scenario_name: Year boundary — December commitment, January execution, fresh annual grant
exposes: a December Normal commitment executes in January under the prior year's budget; the new year's fresh grant funds January's own independent Normal trigger; no double deduction across the boundary

parameters.execution_valuation_rule_note: Declared FIXTURE PARAMETER, not a Baseline execution-price determination. P1-1/OD-04 untouched. Satisfies OD-03.

hand_derived_expectations.note: Hand-reasoned: 2021-12-31 DD=-11% -> NORMAL fires (attributed_month 2021-12, attributed_budget_year 2021), consuming 1.0 of 2021's 12.0-unit grant. It executes on 2022-01-03 (next observation), which is also the first observation of 2022, so the fresh 12.0-unit 2022 grant lands there too (BUDGET_GRANT before EXECUTION in the per-observation processing order) — available becomes 11.0 (2021 remainder) + 12.0 (2022 grant) = 23.0 immediately after the grant, then execution of the December allocation deducts nothing further from `available` (it was already reserved in December) — only `reserved_outstanding` and `executed_units` move. 2022-01-03 itself is DD=-5% -> HIGH, no new January signal that day. 2022-01-04 DD=(88-100)/100=-12% -> NORMAL, January's own first qualifying event -> fires (attributed_month 2022-01, attributed_budget_year 2022), funded from the fresh grant. granted totals 24.0 across both years; no double deduction (verified by ENG-2/INV-11, unaffected by Strategy D).
